title: The additive identity maps to one
statement: Let $k \ge 1$ and write $\omega_k = e^{2\pi i/k}$ for the primitive $k$-th root of unity, and for $a \in \mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$ let its image under the homomorphism $(\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}, +) \to (\mathbb{C}^\times, \cdot)$ be $\omega_k^{a}$. Then the additive identity $0 \in \mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$ maps to $1$; that is, $\omega_k^{0} = 1$.
replaced: The embedding sends zero to one: $\texttt{ZkFourier.toOmega}\ (0 : \mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}) = 1$.
